objectives.textEn: Recognise odd and even functions and their graphs; |x| is even.
Principle of mathematical induction (first principle); prove propositions on finite sums.
Expand binomials with positive integer indices; prove the binomial theorem; summation notation.
Radian measure.
Cosecant, secant, cotangent; identities 1+tan²=sec², 1+cot²=cosec²; simplify with identities.
Compound angle, double angle, product-to-sum and sum-to-product formulae for sine, cosine, tangent.
Definitions and notation of e and the natural logarithm (via lim(1+1/n)^n or the exponential series).
Intuitive concept of the limit of a function; limit theorems (no proofs).
Find limits, including sinθ/θ→1, (e^x-1)/x→1, and limits of rational functions at infinity.
Concept of the derivative; derive elementary functions (C, x^n, √x, sin, cos, e^x, ln x) from first principles.
Sum, product, quotient and chain rules.
Derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions.
Implicit differentiation (incl. logarithmic differentiation).
Second derivative; second derivative test and concavity.
Equations of tangents to a curve.
Maximum and minimum values (local and global).
Sketch polynomial and rational function curves (symmetry, intercepts, extrema, inflexion, asymptotes incl. oblique via division).
Rate of change and optimisation problems.
Concept of indefinite integration.
Properties and formulae for algebraic, trigonometric and exponential functions (incl. sin, cos, sec²).
Applications in mathematical contexts (e.g. geometry).
Integration by substitution.
Trigonometric substitutions for integrals involving a²-x², a²+x², x²+a² forms (as listed in the guide); inverse trig notation and principal values.
Integration by parts (at most twice per integral).
Definite integral as a limit of a sum; dummy variables.
Properties, including odd/even function symmetry results.
Definite integrals of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential functions; Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
Definite integration by substitution.
Definite integration by parts (at most twice).
Area of a plane figure by definite integration.
Volume of a solid of revolution about a coordinate axis or a parallel line (disc method).
Determinants of order 2 and 3; notation |A|, det A.
Concept, operations (addition, scalar multiple, multiplication) and properties of matrices.
Inverses of square matrices of order 2 and 3, and their properties.
Solve 2- and 3-variable linear systems by Cramer's rule, inverse matrices, Gaussian elimination; homogeneous systems have nontrivial solutions iff the coefficient matrix is singular.
Vectors vs scalars; magnitude, zero vector, unit vectors; notation.
Addition, subtraction, scalar multiplication and their properties.
Vectors in the rectangular coordinate system (R² and R³ formulae).
Definition and properties of the scalar (dot) product.
Definition and properties of the vector (cross) product in R³.
Division of a line segment, parallelism, orthogonality, angle between vectors, projection of a vector, triangle area.
Discover and construct knowledge through learning activities; build inquiry, communication and reasoning skills.
